overall_reason: The page's two sign-up buttons, 'LET'S GO ↗' and 'START MAKING MOVES ↗', both jump to the in-page '#workspace' section that 'How it works' also targets, so the main action leads to no sign-up, and the hero's yellow primary on a yellow ground reads quieter than its white secondary.

score.reason: T-WHERE-AM-I fails because the main action and its arrow promise a destination the page does not have (CMP-012, CMP-127), T-PRIMARY-COUNT fails on a secondary louder than the primary (CMP-115), and T-STATE-MATRIX finds one hover, one active and one focus-visible rule (CMP-002).

visitor_mode: Persuade: a one-screen-deep landing page for a team workspace whose goal is a sign-up ('NO CREDIT CARD'). No 00-contract.md; inferred from 'START MAKING MOVES' and 'NO CREDIT CARD. NO BS. JUST BETTER WORK.'

findings.title: Every navigation item and action goes somewhere
findings.where: header 'LET'S GO ↗' and hero 'START MAKING MOVES ↗', 1440 and 375, dom-1440.json
findings.evidence: dom-1440.json gives both buttons href '#workspace', the same in-page anchor as the nav link 'How it works'. No link on the page leads to a sign-up, trial or contact, although the hero says 'NO CREDIT CARD'.
findings.before: The sign-up buttons scroll to the product picture.
findings.after: Both buttons linked to the sign-up page with one label; [DATA NEEDED: the sign-up URL].
findings.why: A visitor ready to start is scrolled down the same page and never reaches a sign-up.

findings.title: One link behaviour site-wide
findings.evidence: Both buttons end in a north-east arrow, the usual mark for a link that leaves the site, but both are in-page anchors ('#workspace'); 'SHOW ME HOW', also an in-page anchor ('#features'), has no arrow.
findings.before: An external-link arrow on buttons that scroll the same page.
findings.after: No arrow on in-page links, or a down arrow if a scroll target is kept; the arrow kept only for links that leave the site.
findings.why: The arrow tells the visitor to expect a new page, and the jump down the same page then reads as a mistake.

findings.title: Secondaries outlined or typographic, never louder than the primary
findings.where: hero buttons, 1440 and 375, fold-1440.png and fold-375.png
findings.evidence: The primary 'START MAKING MOVES ↗' is filled rgb(255, 223, 56) yellow on the hero's yellow ground, so it reads as a black outline; the secondary 'SHOW ME HOW' is white (rgb(255, 255, 255)) with the same black border and offset shadow, so it stands out more against the yellow.
findings.before: The white secondary is the brightest button in the hero.
findings.after: The primary in black with yellow or white text, and the secondary as a plain text link or a yellow outline.
findings.why: The eye goes to 'SHOW ME HOW', not to the sign-up.

findings.title: Every state a control can reach is designed
findings.evidence: declared_states reads 65 readable rules with 1 hover, 1 active and 1 focus-visible rule, 0 hover media queries and 0 disabled rules for three button styles and three nav links.
findings.before: One shared hover and press rule for every control.
findings.after: Each variant with its own hover (one step of its own fill), pressed and focus-visible look, hover inside @media (hover: hover).
findings.why: The hard offset shadows invite a pressed look that only one rule supplies.

strengths: A skip link is the first focus stop, and the logo links to '#top'.
The 375 header keeps the logo and the main action on one line ('LET'S GO ↗'), and the hero buttons stay at label width (fold-375.png).
The hero's checklist window reads as an illustration (C48): it has no controls the capture could click.
not_investigated: Any sign-up flow: none exists on the page; the async capture found no primary action.
The in-page links 'The good stuff' and 'How it works' are not in the 375 header; the page is short, so I did not count it as a T-PHONE-NAV failure.
The footer labels the page 'Fictional product · Impeccable design-pattern example'. The whole page is the exhibit, so its components are judged as the page's own interface.
